This is the Lab Week 5 document for R-DAVIS. Complete the tasks below in this file, then click **Render** and upload the resulting HTML file to Canvas.


This week's questions will have us practicing pivots, conditional statements, and joins with the international environmental agreements data. The codebook at https://ucd-rdavis.github.io/R-DAVIS/data/iea_codebook.md describes every column in all three tables. The data are a simplified subset of the International Environmental Agreements Database Project (https://www.iea.ulaval.ca; Mitchell et al. 2020, *Global Environmental Politics* 20(1): 103–121), prepared for this course.

1. Create a tibble named `agreements` from the iea_agreements.csv file, found at https://ucd-rdavis.github.io/R-DAVIS/data/iea_agreements.csv. Then manipulate `agreements` to create a new dataframe called `agreements_wide` that includes only multilateral agreements, with a column for subject and a column named after every instrument type (Agreement, Amendment, Protocol), with each of these columns containing the mean number of members (`n_members`) of agreements of that instrument type and subject. So every row has a subject and then a mean number of members for every instrument type. The dataframe should be sorted by values in the Agreement column. This question will involve quite a few of the functions you've used so far, and it may be useful to sketch out the steps to get to the final result. Is there an `NA` in your result? What does it mean?

2. Create a dataframe called `multilateral` that contains only the multilateral agreements from `agreements`. Then use the two different functions we laid out for conditional statements, ifelse() and case_when(), to calculate a new size category variable called `size_cat`. For this variable, define the number of members into three categories, where "small" is less than or equal to the 1st quartile of the `n_members` distribution, "medium" is between (but not inclusive) the 1st and 3rd quartile, and "large" is any value greater than or equal to the 3rd quartile. (Hint: the summary() function on a column summarizes the distribution). For ifelse() and case_when(), compare what happens to the `n_members` values of NA, depending on how you specify your arguments.

3. Now bring in the other two tables. Create tibbles named `memberships` and `countries` from https://ucd-rdavis.github.io/R-DAVIS/data/iea_memberships.csv and https://ucd-rdavis.github.io/R-DAVIS/data/iea_countries.csv.
    a. Join `countries` onto `memberships` twice, once with `left_join()` and once with `inner_join()`. How many rows does each result have? Use `anti_join()` to find out which parties in `memberships` have no match in `countries`, and explain in a sentence or two why they don't match.
    b. Using only the rows where a country actually joined an agreement (`year_joined` is not NA), which five countries have joined the most agreements?
    c. Do OECD countries (the wealthy democracies in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) join more multilateral agreements than other countries? Count the number of multilateral agreements each country has joined (again, only rows where `year_joined` is not NA), then compare the average for OECD and non-OECD countries. HINT: you'll need information from all three tables, and a country is in the OECD if its `oecd_joined` is not NA.

BONUS: How might you soft code the values (i.e. not type them in manually) of the 1st and 3rd quartile into your conditional statements in question 2?
